note: a wrong name hanged, the culprit hidden

24.label: Beadle Stromer
24.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Steady: Working beside them, you do not tire.

25.label: Informer: Two-Coats
25.desc: Hal Adornes, known in the taverns as Two-Coats. Works The Market. Meet them on the Ward with Coin for a word.

67.label: A Word in the Right Ear
67.desc: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Instinct, for good. With your Instinct beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Informers bring word sooner.)

76.label: The Fencing-master
76.desc: A gentleman on the Hill, retired from a regiment nobody names, has watched you walk the hard round past his window three nights running. He offers to teach you the rapier. It is not really about the rapier. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Health, for good. With your Health beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: The hard round pays one Coin more: you know where the ground is.)

83.label: The Old Examiner's Method
83.desc: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Witnesses keep half again as long before they forget.)

109.label: The Market
109.desc: Stalls, the weigh-house, pawnbrokers and cutpurses. The pillory stands in the square, and your Watch-house at its edge.

125.label: Petition: The Hole
125.desc: A cell under the Watch-house with a table and one candle. Questioning is faster and draws out more Word. Costs 8 Coin.

127.label: Petition: The Rolls
127.desc: The court's old books, shelved and indexed. Unanswered cases can be opened again in Study. Costs 8 Coin.

128.label: Petition: The Thief-takers' Office
128.desc: A room let to men who know every fence in the city. Put a Case in Attend with 2 Coin and they get the goods back for a cut, without a trial. Some of what they bring back is a frame. Costs 6 Coin.

133.label: Apothecary's Boy Tanner
133.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Slot them into a verb to help. Sharp: Reads raw proof properly even without the right instrument.

135.label: Clerk Visscher
135.desc: Reads a ledger like a romance and a forged hand like a confession. Ink under every nail. Slot them into a verb to help. Sharp: Reads raw proof properly even without the right instrument.

144.label: Protection in Pauw Lane
144.desc: Things have gone wrong at Pauw Lane since the keeper changed: a delivery that never comes on time. Somebody wants a share, and Anneke Sawyer is running out of ways to say no. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. (The Warrens) The Guilds want the culprit shamed in the square or fined, and a brother of the guild not hanged.

145.label: Barbel Tucher
145.desc: Barbel Tucher, the landlord of the arcade. Has pledged the same coat at the Lombard's three times this year. (Accused in: Protection in Pauw Lane)

150.label: The Scene Drawn
150.desc: Forty leaves of Pauw Lane in charcoal, numbered and dated. The room as it was.

152.label: The Sergeant's Patience
152.desc: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. He shows you how he sits down between things: how he lets a case go for the length of a pipe, and comes back to it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Spent Health, Wit and Instinct come back in half the time.)

155.label: A Lombard's Chit
155.desc: A chit from across the river for a coat, redeemed and pledged again. Somebody lives from Friday to Friday.

156.label: What They Want
156.desc: a share. The demand has a shape, and the shape has a name.

158.label: Matthes Sawyer
158.desc: Matthes Sawyer, a stallholder who pays. Smokes a clay pipe of cheap Dutch tobacco, one bowl after another. (Accused in: Protection in Pauw Lane)

159.label: The Warrens
159.desc: Tenements stacked against the wall, and cellars under the cellars. Everyone saw nothing, and everyone knows everything.

160.label: Confessor Fletcher
160.desc: A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God. Slot them into a verb to help. Gentle: Witnesses trust them. A bluff never frightens anyone off.

167.label: The Slashed Awning
167.desc: Cut from the street, an hour before the gate bell, when the lane is still busy. They wanted to be seen.

168.label: Apollonia Tucher
168.desc: Apollonia Tucher, a bravo of the Stews. Has lately paid a carrier for a seat on the wagon to the coast. (Accused in: Protection in Pauw Lane)

169.label: The Council's Letter: Bailiff
169.desc: Watch a door and go in Disguise (Explore), and Deputise a watchman with a case (Attend). Attend on the Council.

171.label: Blood Court: Jörg Cooper
171.desc: Jörg Cooper stands before the Blood Court for Protection in Holzschuher Lane. The charge looked like full proof.

175.label: A Patrician's Letter
175.desc: A letter under a good seal. The writer would take it kindly if the Examiner found cause to search the house of Nan Kuiper, a merchant of the Hill. Three Coin are mentioned, delicately. Put it in Attend to oblige, or let it lie.

176.label: Letter: Sergeant of the Watch
176.desc: Thirty years with a halberd. Has seen this before. Has seen everything before, and hanged some of it. Costs 5 Coin.

ask.label: A shut door
ask.text: One house will not open to the Watch. It opens to Coin. Shut, it keeps what it knows.

story.title: Sleep
story.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

c10.title: Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop

vars.item: the strongbox, opened rather than forced

suspects.name: Bartel Claesz
suspects.motive: The nephew was cut out of the will a week ago, loudly, at table.

suspects.name: Regina Schmidt
suspects.motive: The partnership is drowning in debt, and a theft is a loss the guild will forgive.

suspects.name: Endres Claesz
suspects.motive: Let go without a letter, and still talking of it in every tavern in the Stews.

result.label: The Tobacco Named
result.text: Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars.

items.label: Marks on the Sill
items.text: The print of a hand on the whitewash. Faint, but there.

result.label: The Hand Read
result.text: Under vinegar and the red umbrella the hand comes up whole: a thumb with a scar across it. Good enough for the Court.

items.label: The Second Key
items.text: The strongbox was opened, not forced. Three people have a key. One of them lent it.

items.label: The Carrier's Chit
items.text: A carrier's chit for a place on Friday's wagon to the coast. One way. Someone is planning to leave.

witnesses: the woman at the casement opposite

c40.title: Fire at the Hobson Print-shop

vars.time: on the night the rent was due

suspects.name: Hans de Witt
suspects.motive: The clerk had been skimming from the books, and the books were in the counting-room.

suspects.name: Els Vos
suspects.motive: The fire-setter has been examined about three fires before. Never charged.
suspects.alibi: a wedding, and forty guests who remember the dancing

suspects.name: Matthes Holzschuher
suspects.motive: The building was pledged for three times its worth, and the owner was ruined.

items.label: A Hobnail Scar
items.text: A deep gouge at the foot of the door, the kind a hobnailed boot makes. A big boot, and a kick.

items.label: The Message
items.text: a list of other shops. This was not the first, and it was not meant to be the last.

items.label: The Smell Under the Smoke
items.text: The floor stinks of lamp-oil under the char.

result.label: The Oil Named
result.text: Rape-oil cut with spirit, a blend sold by one chandler in the Abbey Close.

items.label: A lit taper dropped carefully
items.text: What the fire started with. Cheap, and handled.

result.label: The Hand on the Kindling
result.text: A clean thumb on the one part that did not burn.

witnesses: a child who could not sleep

c106.title: Protection in Holzschuher Lane

vars.time: on the first of the month
vars.detail: a cart that stands outside until it is paid

suspects.name: Dirck Barker
suspects.motive: The bravo collects the money, and keeps a share.

suspects.name: Grete van der Meer
suspects.motive: The sergeant's round is exactly the streets being squeezed.
suspects.alibi: a game of tables with a sergeant of the Watch

suspects.name: Jörg Cooper
suspects.motive: Frightened tenants accept a higher rent. The landlord knows it.

items.label: The Victim's Account
items.text: Jörg van der Meer tells you everything, hands shaking, and begs you not to write their name down.

items.label: The Collectors
items.text: a cart that stands outside until it is paid. Everybody has seen them. Nobody has seen them.

items.label: The Round
items.text: They collect in the same order every time, and Jörg van der Meer's stall was on the list. a receipt book would tell you who else is.

items.label: An Inked Thumb
items.text: A thumbprint, perfect, in printer's ink on the white of the doorframe.

witnesses: the woman who keeps the cookshop

vars.detail: a delivery that never comes on time

suspects.name: Barbel Tucher
suspects.motive: Frightened tenants accept a higher rent. The landlord knows it.

suspects.name: Matthes Sawyer
suspects.motive: The stallholder who pays gets a discount for pointing out who does not.

items.text: A chit from across the river for a coat, redeemed and pledged again. Somebody lives from Friday to Friday.

journal.title: Week 11
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 3. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. A letter under a good seal waits on your desk. It asks nothing outright. A letter of service lands on your desk: Sergeant of the Watch. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Whatever you were working on is gone before you finish. The city does not wait. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Taken: Jörg Cooper
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Sebald Tanner walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Bailiff. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: The Informer's Brother: Send the Watch as planned
journal.text: The brother is taken. Your informer stops meeting your eye. (Standing rises; Vendetta)

journal.title: The Informer's Brother
journal.text: Your informer asks a favour, the first they have ever asked. Their brother runs untaxed wine through the Water-gate. The Watch is due there on Thursday. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Pauw Lane. You find: The Slashed Awning. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Apollonia Tucher. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Jörg Cooper, the landlord of the arcade. It has to be.

journal.title: Week 10
journal.text: You cannot pay your lodging. The landlord puts your chest in the lane at prime. You sleep in the Watch-house, on the bench. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: An Alibi
journal.text: You try Grete van der Meer's story: a game of tables with a sergeant of the Watch. It will want checking.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Claes Fletcher takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Pauw Lane. You find: A Lombard's Chit, What They Want, Bad Luck, Regularly. The first name in the casebook: Matthes Sawyer. The case takes you to The Warrens. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Lienhard Stromer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Corroborated Account
journal.text: The body of the thing and the words of the witnesses finally agree. They point the same way. You know what kind of person. Not yet which.

journal.title: An Insight: The Sergeant's Patience
journal.text: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. He shows you how he sits down between things: how he lets a case go for the length of a pipe, and comes back to it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with Pauw Lane before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Two-Coats counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Protection in Holzschuher Lane.

journal.title: Week 9
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. A letter of service lands on your desk: Confessor. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Commission from The Guilds: Protection in Pauw Lane
journal.text: Things have gone wrong at Pauw Lane since the keeper changed: a delivery that never comes on time. Somebody wants a share, and Anneke Sawyer is running out of ways to say no. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. The Guilds want the culprit shamed in the square or fined, and a brother of the guild not hanged.

journal.title: Delivered: The Apothecary's Key
journal.text: It arrives by carrier in a crate with the wrong name on it. It works perfectly.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Two-Coats counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Protection in Holzschuher Lane.

journal.title: Entered
journal.text: Four hours with the quill. By the end, even the parts that were not quite by the Carolina read as if they were.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Holzschuher Lane. You find: The Victim's Account, The Collectors, The Round. The first name in the casebook: Dirck Barker. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Griet Visscher takes the oath at the Watch-house door. Reads a ledger like a romance and a forged hand like a confession. Ink under every nail.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Sebald Tanner takes the oath at the Watch-house door. Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted.

journal.title: A Hot Dinner
journal.text: Mutton, bread, small beer, and a second helping. Your hands stop shaking somewhere around the pudding.

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: The Rival Exposed
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. The Council reads the file in silence and sends the Harbourmaster's Examiner back to the Customs House. Your name is spoken in the chamber, warmly for once.

journal.title: Promoted: Sworn Examiner
journal.text: You swear the oath in the Council chamber with your hand on the Carolina, and the clerk writes your name under the last Examiner's, which has a line through it. You are now Sworn Examiner. A magistrate will seal a Writ for you (an Accused with cause, in Explore), and the Council sends you more. The Council will send you up to 3 cases at once, and pay 2 a week.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with Holzschuher Lane before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: Week 8
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. A letter of service lands on your desk: Clerk. The ledger: 1 conviction; 1 open; 16 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Fire: Matthes Holzschuher
journal.text: The staff is broken, and the fire follows, before the whole city. It takes most of the morning. The crowd is very quiet by the end, and so is the Market for a week after. The underworld learns your name from it.

journal.title: Ahead of the Crier
journal.text: "Something is going to happen," says Two-Coats. "Soon." Keep the warning on the table: when it comes, you will be ready for it.

journal.title: Guilty: Matthes Holzschuher
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Matthes Holzschuher is convicted of Fire at the Hobson Print-shop, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. A Council family in the dock. The Hill will not forgive it, and the Stews will not forget it. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached. At the court door Ursel Kramer presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee. But one detail belongs to no one in the case: a small mason's mark, three strokes, cut where the crime began. You have seen it before.

journal.title: Condemned: Matthes Holzschuher
journal.text: Matthes Holzschuher goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, Banished, The Sword, The Fire. The Council will follow your word, or its custom.

journal.title: The Market
journal.text: The stallholders know your face now. The Quarter is yours to walk: put it in Explore with Health for a round, or with a case to look for its people there.

journal.title: A Commission from The Council: Protection in Holzschuher Lane
journal.text: Stallholders around Holzschuher Lane have been paying for "protection" on the first of the month, collected by a cart that stands outside until it is paid. Jörg van der Meer refused, and lost their awning. Somewhere there is a receipt book. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. The Council wants it answered within 21 days, and would take it kindly if Jörg Cooper, of a Council family, were not the name.

journal.title: Nothing Tonight
journal.text: Two-Coats takes the coin and has nothing for it. "Next week," they say.

journal.title: Marked: Two-Coats
journal.text: Somebody in the Warrens has asked, by name, who Two-Coats's friend at the Watch-house is. They stop coming to the bench. Guard them in Attend with a watchman, or the next time they are asked it will not be politely.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: A Long Rest
journal.text: A week of nothing. Long walks outside the walls. Small beer and bread. Your hands stop shaking on the fourth day. On the seventh you want to go back to the Watch-house, which is either a good sign or a very bad one.

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk: Pocket it
journal.text: Silver is silver. Somebody now believes you can be bought, because you can. (+3 Coin; the Council's eye)

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk
journal.text: Nobody saw who left it. Three Coin, good silver, and a note with the name of a case on it and nothing else. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Whatever you were working on is gone before you finish. The city does not wait.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Lienhard Stromer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: The Rope: Bartel Claesz
journal.text: The staff is broken. Bartel Claesz hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. The crowd goes home satisfied. The Bishop's chaplain will remember that you were asked.

journal.title: A Weakness Found
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. They will be careful for a week. One more, and you will have them.

journal.title: The Condemned's Wife: Take the purse and say the word
journal.text: The word goes to the Council. So, in time, does the story of the purse. (+3 Coin; Mercy; the Council's eye)

journal.title: The Condemned's Wife
journal.text: She waits at the Watch-house door with a purse, three Coin in it, and asks only that a word for mercy reach the Council before it speaks. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Week 7
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: 1 conviction; 0 open; 8 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Taken: Matthes Holzschuher
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Nothing Tonight
journal.text: Two-Coats takes the coin and has nothing for it. "Next week," they say.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Sworn Examiner. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Guilty: Bartel Claesz
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Bartel Claesz is convicted of Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached. At the court door Margery Sattler presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee.

journal.title: Condemned: Bartel Claesz
journal.text: Bartel Claesz goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Bishop's Plea.

journal.title: An Insight: The Old Examiner's Method
journal.text: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Matthes Holzschuher, the building's owner. It has to be.

journal.title: Fever
journal.text: You stand in the Market outside the Watch-house for an hour and cannot make yourself go in. Your hands will not stop shaking. You need rest, and soon.

journal.title: Nothing Doing
journal.text: Rain, cressets, and the ring of pattens on wet stone. Nothing you can use. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: A stallholder shakes your hand. A boy spits at your boots. An ordinary round. Alone in the lane, and it wore you out.

journal.title: An Insight: The Fencing-master
journal.text: A gentleman on the Hill, retired from a regiment nobody names, has watched you walk the hard round past his window three nights running. He offers to teach you the rapier. It is not really about the rapier. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Rape-oil cut with spirit, a blend sold by one chandler in the Abbey Close. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Harbourmaster's Examiner
journal.text: Piet Wieland has the Harbourmaster's letter and a desk in the Customs House. The Harbourmaster wants the Council to see it has a choice. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: Wouter Kessler keeps begging your pardon for wasting your time. They are not wasting it. "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles."

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Two-Coats counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Fire at the Hobson Print-shop.

journal.title: An Insight: A Word in the Right Ear
journal.text: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Taken: Bartel Claesz
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Hobson Print-shop. You find: The Smell Under the Smoke. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Hans de Witt. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: A Word from Two-Coats
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Fire at the Hobson Print-shop. Two-Coats does not sign things.

journal.title: The Cough Clears
journal.text: Bitter bark in wine, two days sweating under every blanket you own, and on the third morning the river smells like a river again.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Lienhard Stromer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Bartel Claesz Cracks
journal.text: You slide The Carrier's Chit across the table. Bartel Claesz's composure goes, all at once, like a dam breaking.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Hobson Print-shop. You find: A Hobnail Scar, The Message. The first name in the casebook: Matthes Holzschuher.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door: Give her a Coin
journal.text: The child gets bread. She tells you who came and went, and the clerks get a story about you. (The Crowd and Dread ease; her word on the case)

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door
journal.text: A woman with a child on her hip has been at the Watch-house door since prime. She does not ask for anything. She just stands there, where the Council's clerks can see her, and she has seen everyone who passed. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sickness
journal.text: A cough from the river, a heat behind the eyes. The Warrens give it to everyone in the end. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Lienhard Stromer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Bartel Claesz, a nephew of the house. It has to be.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with the Hobson Print-shop before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: The Confessor: Leave the seal alone
journal.text: He is grateful, and says so where the Bishop can hear it. (The Bishop's favour)

journal.title: The Confessor
journal.text: A priest of the parish asks for a word. Someone told him something under the seal, and it is eating him. He will not break the seal. He might point. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Cleared: Els Vos
journal.text: Els Vos has an answer, and it is a good one: a wedding, and forty guests who remember the dancing. They are cleared.

journal.title: A Witness Moves On
journal.text: Witness: the Tiler has left the city. Whatever they saw went with them.

journal.title: Week 4
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Overheard
journal.text: At the conduit you hear someone talking about Fire at the Hobson Print-shop. They were there. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: A stallholder shakes your hand. A boy spits at your boots. An ordinary round. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Protection," says Two-Coats, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: A Commission from The Council: Fire at the Hobson Print-shop
journal.text: Somebody set fire to the Hobson Print-shop on the night the rent was due. It started with a lit taper dropped carefully. The message came the next morning: a list of other shops. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name. The Council wants it answered within 18 days, and would take it kindly if Matthes Holzschuher, of a Council family, were not the name.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Stromer's Pawnshop. You find: The Carrier's Chit.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 3
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 3 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Stromer's Pawnshop. You find: The Second Key. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Endres Claesz. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Lienhard Stromer walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Fire," says Two-Coats, "in The Warrens. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars.

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother: Give him the week, and his wage
journal.text: He goes. The others see it. (Standing rises; Dread eases)

journal.title: The Watchman's Mother
journal.text: One of your watchmen asks for the week: his mother is dying in the Warrens and there is nobody else. The round will be short a man. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Stromer's Pawnshop. You find: Pipe Ash in the Study, Marks on the Sill. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Bartel Claesz. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan: Watch who leaves
journal.text: You let it burn out and watch the door. The potboy sees you watching, and sees a living in it. (An Informer at the Swan)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan
journal.text: The round passes the Swan as two carters go through its window. The tapster is shouting your name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Lienhard Stromer takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Stromer's Pawnshop. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Regina Schmidt. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: The Tiler's Word: A Coin for his trouble
journal.text: He saw a face, and he will say so again where it counts. (A Witness who saw it)

journal.title: The Tiler's Word
journal.text: A tiler was on his ladder across the lane when it happened, mending a roof that did not need mending. He says so to anyone with a coin, and now he is saying it to you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with Stromer's Pawnshop before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: Somebody's Casebook
journal.text: The drawer of your new desk still has the last examiner's quills in it, and a leaf torn from a casebook with one word underlined three times. You put it in your coat and open the first case.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Stromer's Pawnshop
journal.text: Margery Sattler is not sure when it happened: during the wedding downstairs. Only the cellar hatch was touched, and only the strongbox, opened rather than forced taken. A neighbour reports seeing a guest who left early. Somebody knew the house.
